page: Amazon Web Services r8i-flex.8xlarge is a memory-optimized cloud server powered by the AWS Nitro System and Intel Xeon 6975P-C processors. Operating on the x86_64 architecture, this instance features 32 virtual CPUs derived from 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading at clock speeds up to 3.9 GHz. The CPU subsystem is equipped with a large 480 MB L3 cache and supports specialized instruction sets including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX). It is configured with 256 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory operating at 7 GHz, maintaining an 8 GB memory-to-vCPU ratio.

Hardware architecture highlights include zero local storage devices, requiring attached network storage such as Amazon EBS for persistent data, and an 8 Gbps baseline network bandwidth profile. The underlying processor includes hardware support for cryptographic operations with AES, VAES, and SHA-NI, as well as enterprise memory control and isolation features. The instance does not include dedicated graphics processing units.

Benchmark assessments show competitive general compute throughput, reflected by a multi-core Geekbench score of 17,619 and a PassMark CPU score of 51,371.12. Cryptographic acceleration and compression exhibit strong results, reaching 34.39 GB/sec in single-threaded gzip compression and 223.13 GB/sec in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression. Due to AMX instruction support, CPU-driven LLM inference performs well for smaller models, achieving 385.79 tokens per second on 135M parameter models, though larger parameter sets encounter architectural compute bounds.

The r8i-flex variant implements a burstable CPU allocation model, delivering a cost-effective alternative to standard memory-optimized instances when sustained peak CPU performance is not required. By packaging 256 GB of DDR5 RAM with flexible compute thresholds, the server is suitable for memory-heavy databases, Redis caches, batch data processing, and large-scale web serving tiers.
description: Amazon Web Services r8i-flex.8xlarge is a memory-optimized instance operating on the AWS Nitro System and powered by an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it delivers 32 burstable vCPUs across 16 physical cores running up to 3.9 GHz, backed by 480 MB of L3 cache and 256 GB of 7 GHz DDR5 memory. The instance features no local disk storage, relying on networked block volumes, and includes an 8 Gbps baseline network interface. Benchmark results indicate strong cryptographic performance, multi-threaded decompression throughput of 223.13 GB/sec, and efficient small-model machine learning inference via Intel AMX instructions. Due to its burstable processor allocation and substantial memory capacity, this instance offers resource efficiency for in-memory caching systems, intermediate database servers, web application backends, and data processing pipelines.
